Upper-Tail Table for a Discrete Distribution

Source: R/numerical_fallbacks.R
disc_upper_table.Rd

Builds \(S(k) = P(Y > k)\) over the support from its lower bound by summing the mass from the top of the table downward, so that each value is a sum of the terms above \(k\) and keeps its relative accuracy however small it is. The table grows by doubling until it reaches the upper bound of the support or until the mass beyond its last point is negligible, below \(10^{-17}\) of the probability that the caller needs.

Usage

disc_upper_table(distrib, theta, need_p = NULL, need_k = NULL, kmax = 1e+06)

Arguments

distrib

An object inheriting from class "discrete_distrib".

theta

A named list of parameters, each of length 1.

need_p

The probability that the caller compares with the table: the table grows until the neglected mass is below \(10^{-17}\) of it.

need_k

A support point whose upper tail the caller reads: the table grows until it passes this point and the neglected mass is below \(10^{-17}\) of the mass above it.

kmax

A ceiling on the table size.

Value

A list with the support points ks and the upper-tail probabilities S, of the same length.

Details

The mass beyond the last point \(K\) is bounded by the geometric series \(f(K)\,r/(1-r)\) with \(r = f(K)/f(K-1)\), which holds where the ratio of consecutive masses decreases, as it does in the tail of every shipped count family, and is added to every entry. A ratio that has not fallen below one keeps the table growing up to kmax points, after which the function warns.

See also

disc_cum_table(), the table of the lower tail; distrib_cdf.discrete_distrib() and distrib_quantile.discrete_distrib(), which read it.
